messages.subject: Another warning message
messages.body_plain:
Hello guys,

I hope you're enjoying this holiday.

I have another warning message when trying to fit unidimensional and bifactor models. In this case, my dataset is pretty small (n = 200), so I believe this might be the source of the message. My data has no missing values, is non-normal and comes from a five-point Likert scale with 27 items. As far as I think, there are no issues with the identification of the models.

I would appreciate your valuable help. Thanks in advance.

Here is my code:

unid <- 'GF =~ x1+x2+x6+x7+x8+x14+x15+x16+x18+x19+x23+x25+x27+x28+x29+x30+x31+x35+x38+x24+x33+x36+x39+x22+x34+x37+x41'

bifa <- '
GF =~ x1+x2+x6+x7+x8+x14+x15+x16+x18+x19+x23+x25+x27+x28+x29+x30+x31+x35+x38+x24+x33+x36+x39+x22+x34+x37+x41
F1 =~ x1+x2+x6+x7+x8+x14+x15+x16+x18+x19+x23+x25+x27+x28+x29+x30+x31+x35+x38
F2 =~ x24+x33+x36+x39
F3 =~ x22+x34+x37+x41
F1 ~~ 0*F2
F1 ~~ 0*F3
F2 ~~ 0*F3
GF ~~ 0*F1
GF ~~ 0*F2
GF ~~ 0*F3'

unid.fit <- cfa(unid, data = mydata, ordered = paste0("x", 1:42))
bifa.fit <- cfa(bifa, data = mydata, ordered = paste0("x", 1:42))

The warning messages are:

1: In lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!

2: In lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!

3: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov) does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue (= 1.504327e-17) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

messages.subject: Trying to estimate the stability of a variable using Lavaan.
messages.subject_clean: Trying to estimate the stability of a variable using Lavaan.
messages.body_plain:
Dear colleagues,

Hope you're all doing well during this difficult year.

Disclaimer: I'm new to Lavaan and SEM, though I consider myself to be an advanced R user.

I'm trying to use a measurement model to estimate the stability of a variable across multiple measurements. . Largely, I'm trying to approximate the results obtained using a dynamic model approach. For those not familiar with it, dynamic panels are, basically, a first differences model, using the lagged levels of the variable as an instrument In a nutshell, the closer  to 0 the value of the slope, the more stable the variable is.

I seek to do a similar thing using Lavaan but I'm unsure about how to go about it–unsure about how to interpret the results or even if what I'm doing is right, even after reading the Lavaan tutorial <https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/tutorial.pdf>.

Suppose I have a three wave panel, where variable x is measured at t1, t2, and t3. I simply want to get at the stability of x, for now–i.e., the simplest possible model. Here's what I have, so far:

mod <- "
  x =~ t1 + t2 + t3
"
fit <- sem(mod, data = data)

I get results, but I'm unsure about how to interpret them. What is the hypotheses being tested in the parameters?

Per reading the tutorial, I tried using labels to make t2 equal to t3, but I'm not at all sure this is what I want. I'm also unsure whether I should use growth(), rather than sem(), though they do not seem to be very different from each other.

Any help would be much appreciated.

Thank you and happy holydays to all,
-- Lucas de Abreu Maia, he/him/his
Ph.D. candidate | Department of Political Science | University of California, San Diego
lucasamaia.com <http://lucasamaia.com/>

PS: I apologize if this message accidentally is posted twice. I tried to email the group yesterday but it didn't go through, apparently.

Chester

You dont have latent variables here, and are adding a bunch of constraints that I dont think make sense. If the idea its to use a single indicator variable to define latent variables, i this case you will reach the same withput the single indicator variable, just suing th variables directly

Model.missing <- '
a ~~ b + c + d
b ~~  c + d
c ~~ d

m ~ a + b + c + d
'

Modeling.missing = cfa(Model.missing, data = Dataset, estimator = "MLR", missing="fiml")
summary(Modeling.missing, standardized=T)

In the Est column you will have the covariance estimates, and in the std.all column you will have the correlation estimates

If you want to use single indicator factors need to defined them like this for example
'
ph_a =~ 1*a
ph_a ~~ NA*ph_a
ph_a ~0*1
a ~~ 0*a
'
In this form, I am moin the item variance to the latent factor variance, and the mean estimated at the item level. You can estimated in different ways, like the next one.
'
ph_a =~ NA*a
ph_a ~~ 1*ph_a
ph_a ~0*1
a ~~ 0*a
'
This one standardized the latent variable and the factor loadings will be the indicator standard deviation. Depends how you want to interpret this phantom latent variable.

But for the simple example, you presented, I dont think his would be neccesary

messages.body_plain:
Hi
First instal semTools then After fitting your model in lavaan use reliability function from semTools to compute AVE and CR. for example:

library(lavaan)
library(semTools)

CFA.2F <-'
F1=~ PVD2+PVD5+PVD6+PVD8+PVD10+PVD12+PVD14
F2=~ PVD1+PVD3+PVD4+PVD7+PVD9+PVD11+PVD13+PVD15
'
CFA.2F.sus <- cfa(CFA.2F, data = sus1,std.lv <http://std.lv> = TRUE,ordered=names(sus1), estimator = "WLSMV")
summary(CFA.2F.sus , fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
# what you need
print(reliability(CFA.2F.sus,return.total = TRUE), digits = 3)

Dear Yves,

do you still require such data?
I encountered the same issue with 1 out of 20 imputed datasets consisting of ~630k observations, which i'd gladly contribute:

lavaan:::lav_bvmix_cor_twostep_fit() throws warning; estimation did not always converge

polycor::polyserial does not throw any warning.

The estimates returned by both routines are very close.

Anyway - in the context of multiple imputation, the problem can easily be bypassed by manually excluding the specific dataset(s) that throw the warning. For future releases of the semtools-package it might be worthwhile to automatize this procedure. Currently, all datasets seems to be used for pooling irrespective of this warning.
